{{Short description|Type of dynamical system}}
In the theory of [[dynamical systems]], a '''bailout embedding''' is a system defined as<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cartwright | first1=Julyan H. E. | author1-link = Julyan Cartwright| last2=Magnasco | first2=Marcelo O. | last3=Piro | first3=Oreste | title=Bailout embeddings, targeting of invariant tori, and the control of Hamiltonian chaos | journal=Physical Review E | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=65 | issue=4 | date=2002-04-03 | issn=1063-651X | doi=10.1103/physreve.65.045203 | page=045203(R)| pmid=12005907 |arxiv=nlin/0111005| bibcode=2002PhRvE..65d5203C | s2cid=23498762 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Tuval | first1=Idan | last2=Piro | first2=Oreste | title=Bailout Embedding as a Blowout Bifurcation | journal=Progress of Theoretical Physics Supplement | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=150 | year=2003 | issn=0375-9687 | doi=10.1143/ptps.150.465 | pages=465–468| bibcode=2003PThPS.150..465T |doi-access=free| hdl=10261/15339 | hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Shan | first1=Zhang | last2=Shi-Ping | first2=Yang | last3=Hu | first3=Liu | title=Targeting of Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser Orbits by the Bailout Embedding Method in Two Coupled Standard Maps | journal=Chinese Physics Letters | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=23 | issue=5 | date=2006-04-28 | issn=0256-307X | doi=10.1088/0256-307x/23/5/014 | pages=1114–1117| bibcode=2006ChPhL..23.1114Z | s2cid=250847203 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Thyagu | first1=N. Nirmal | last2=Gupte | first2=Neelima | title=Clustering, chaos, and crisis in a bailout embedding map | journal=Physical Review E | volume=76 | issue=4 | date=2007-10-22 | issn=1539-3755 | doi=10.1103/physreve.76.046218 | article-number=046218| pmid=17995093 |arxiv=0707.3102| bibcode=2007PhRvE..76d6218T | s2cid=1801240 }}</ref>
:<math>
\begin{align}
&\frac{d}{dt} (u-f(x)) = -k(x) (u-f(x)), \\[8pt]
&\frac{dx}{dt}  = u.
\end{align}
</math>
Here the function ''k''(''x'') < 0 on a [[set (mathematics)|set]] of unwanted [[orbit (dynamics)|orbits]]; otherwise ''k''(''x'') > 0. The [[trajectory|trajectories]] of the full system of a bailout embedding ''bail out''—that is, detach—from the [[embedding]], into a larger space, in which they move around. If, after some time these orbits arrive at a [[stability theory|stable]] neighbourhood of the embedding, ''k''(''x'') > 0, they collapse once more onto the embedding; that is, onto the original [[Dynamics (mechanics)|dynamics]]. The bailout embedding forms in this way an enlarged version of the [[dynamical system]], one in which particular sets of orbits are cut from the asymptotic or [[limit set]], while maintaining the dynamics of a different set of orbits—the wanted set—as [[attractor]]s of the larger dynamical system. With a choice of ''k''(''x'') =&nbsp;−(''γ''&nbsp;+&nbsp;∇''f''), these dynamics are seen to detach from unstable regions such as [[saddle point]]s in [[conservative system]]s.

One important application of the bailout embedding concept is to [[divergence-free]] [[Flow (mathematics)|flows]]; the most important class of these are [[Hamiltonian system]]s.
